name: Grand Canyon Rim-to-River
tagline: For backpackers hiking a corridor-trail rim-to-river route with nights at Bright Angel, Havasupai Gardens or Cottonwood campgrounds.
description: Assumes a 2-3 night corridor backpacking trip on the Bright Angel, South Kaibab or North Kaibab trails in spring or fall for a small group holding a backcountry permit. Covers the permit lottery, heat and water logistics, the no-fire rule and critter-proof food storage. Summer trips need pre-dawn starts, more water and salty food; winter trips need traction devices. Check current trail and water closures before you leave.
season: Mar-May and Sept-Nov best; summer extreme heat; winter ice near the rims
considerations: Backcountry permits run through a Recreation.gov early-access lottery (two-week window ending the 1st of the month, four months ahead) with remaining dates opening on the 1st; $10 application plus $15 per person per night below the rim (NPS, as of 2026).
Corridor campgrounds allow 2 nights per campground per hike (4 nights Nov 15-Feb 28) and 7 nights max per use area; the permit must be in the trip leader's possession.

Inner-canyon temperatures often exceed 105 F in summer; do not hike between 10 am and 4 pm, eat double your normal carbohydrates and salty food, and drink to thirst to avoid both dehydration and hyponatremia.

Corridor water depends on the Transcanyon Pipeline and shuts off with little notice. As of Sept 28, 2026 all inner-canyon water was off and Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel and Cottonwood campgrounds were closed by flash-flood damage; check Key Hiking Messages first.
Wood and charcoal fires are prohibited (stoves only); burning, burying or leaving toilet paper is prohibited, so pack it out.
Every corridor campsite has a metal food storage can and pack pole; ravens, ringtails and squirrels raid unsecured packs. Pets and drones are prohibited below the rim.
Climbing out gains about 5,000 ft; plan on twice as long to hike up as down. Hypothermia and heat illness have been treated on the same day.

items.text: Backcountry permit covering every night and use area
items.note: Early-access lottery on Recreation.gov four months ahead; cancellations bookable up to 5 days out (as of 2026).

items.text: Permit printed and carried by the trip leader
Park entrance pass
Check Key Hiking Messages for closures, water status and heat risk
items.note: Pipeline breaks and flash floods closed corridor campgrounds in 2026.

items.text: Itinerary left with a contact; park 24-hour emergency number (928-638-7805) saved
Rim campground or lodging for the night before
Trailhead shuttle plan (e.g., down South Kaibab, up Bright Angel)
Phantom Ranch meals or lodging if wanted
items.note: Reserved separately through the lodge concessioner; sells out far ahead.

items.text: Capacity for 3-4 liters per person plus extra for dry stretches
Water filter or tablets in case the taps are off
items.note: Natural sources are scarce; know where the next one is.

items.text: Electrolyte mix or salt tablets
Salty snacks and double your normal calories
Spray bottle or bandana to wet down
Sun umbrella
Pre-dawn start plan; no hiking 10 am-4 pm in heat
Tent or tarp
items.note: Campsites have picnic tables and pack poles.

items.text: Sleeping bag suited to the season
items.note: River nights run 74-104 F in summer and 38-59 F in winter.

items.text: Sleeping pad
Lightweight tarp or emergency shelter for the day pack
Broken-in boots or shoes with good soles
Light-colored, loose clothing (cotton is fine in summer heat)
Wide-brimmed hat and sunglasses
Fleece or puffy for cold rim mornings
Rain shell
Spare socks
Microspikes for icy upper trails (Nov-Apr)
Warm hat and gloves in winter
Camp sandals
Backpacking stove and fuel (no wood or charcoal fires)
Pot and utensils
Meals for each day plus one extra
Use the metal food storage cans; keep packs zipped against ravens and squirrels
Map or trail guide
Headlamp with spare batteries
First aid kit with blister care and duct tape
Whistle, signal mirror and phone
items.note: Emergency phones exist at corridor campgrounds; cell coverage is spotty.

items.text: Sunscreen
Trekking poles
Satellite messenger
Pocket knife
Know the signs of heat illness and hyponatremia
Bags to pack out toilet paper
Use campground toilets; cathole only where none exist
Trash bag; carry out all trash
No fires of any kind; stove only
Stay on the trail; no shortcutting switchbacks
Leave pets and drones at home
